question:
An investigator is studying the effects of hyperphosphatemia on calcium homeostasis. A high-dose phosphate infusion is administered intravenously to a healthy subject over the course of 3 hours. Which of the following sets of changes is most likely to occur in response to the infusion?
 $$$ Serum parathyroid hormone %%% Serum total calcium %%% Serum calcitriol %%% Urine phosphate $$$?
analysis: Hyperphosphatemia can lead to a decrease in serum calcium levels due to the formation of calcium-phosphate complexes, which can precipitate and decrease free calcium levels. In response to low serum calcium levels, parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion is typically increased to help maintain calcium homeostasis. PTH acts to increase serum calcium levels by promoting bone resorption and enhancing renal calcium reabsorption. Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, is also involved in calcium homeostasis and is regulated by PTH. Increased phosphate levels in the urine may occur as the body tries to excrete the excess phosphate load.
